meta.notes_for_ui: Cycle day 3 (menstrual phase). Priority: more energy. Goal: performance. Morning training preference.

weekly_focus.headline: Steady energy and quality work without digging a fatigue hole
weekly_focus.primary_goal: Maintain performance through consistent, controlled effort across classes
weekly_focus.secondary_goal: Support energy levels and recovery while cravings are higher
weekly_focus.why_this_week: Early menstrual phase often benefits from slightly more conservative intensity so you can keep quality high and stay consistent without overreaching.

distribution.label: easy
distribution.description: Use classes where you leave feeling better than you started, with breathing under control and minimal soreness expected.

distribution.label: moderate
distribution.description: Prioritize steady, repeatable effort where form and pacing stay consistent and you could do a bit more if needed.

distribution.label: hard
distribution.description: Keep hard efforts short and selective, only if energy feels stable and recovery is on track.

class_selection_rules.rule: Consider choosing classes that feel predictable and technique-focused when energy is lower.
class_selection_rules.example: A strength class with controlled pacing instead of a highly competitive HIIT format.

class_selection_rules.rule: If you choose a harder class, consider keeping your effort controlled rather than chasing top-end intensity.
class_selection_rules.example: Staying in a strong-but-manageable zone and avoiding repeated all-out pushes.

modality_guidance.theme: Quality strength with clean technique and controlled pacing
how_to_apply_in_classes: Lean toward moderate effort where form stays crisp and repeatable
Favor sessions that feel balanced rather than maximal or grindy
modality_guidance.intensity_notes: A steady, medium-hard feel tends to support performance without draining energy this week.
what_to_avoid: anything that creates excessive soreness that lingers for days

modality_guidance.theme: Strategic HIIT that boosts energy without wiping you out
how_to_apply_in_classes: Treat intensity as adjustable and aim for strong, controlled bursts rather than all-out efforts
Keep output consistent across the class instead of spiking early and fading
modality_guidance.intensity_notes: If energy is good, a small amount of hard work can fit, but keeping most HIIT at moderate effort usually supports better recovery.
what_to_avoid: stacking multiple high-intensity classes too close together
repeated all-out pushing when you feel flat

how_to_apply_in_classes: Use Pilates as a way to feel more aligned and less tense rather than as a fatigue-builder
Emphasize smooth control and breathing over intensity
modality_guidance.intensity_notes: Easy-to-moderate is a good fit to preserve energy while improving movement quality.
what_to_avoid: turning it into a high-strain session

modality_guidance.theme: Cardio that restores energy and keeps rhythm
how_to_apply_in_classes: Consider steady, conversational-effort cardio as the baseline choice
If choosing a faster-paced cardio class, keep the effort smooth and sustainable
modality_guidance.intensity_notes: Easy-to-moderate cardio can support energy and recovery without adding much stress.
what_to_avoid: extended high-intensity efforts if sleep or recovery feels off
pushing pace when breathing feels disproportionally hard early on

downshift_steps: Shift class choices toward easy/moderate formats and reduce the number of hard moments
Bias toward Pilates or steady cardio to protect energy while staying consistent

swap_examples.why: Supports energy and recovery while keeping training consistent.
Maintains performance focus with less recovery cost.

upshift_steps: Let one class (at most) lean into the hard end while keeping the rest controlled
Increase effort by a small margin while keeping technique and pacing stable
guardrails: Avoid turning multiple classes into maximal-effort days
If soreness or fatigue lingers beyond 24–48 hours, keep the next class easier
